h1: Fullrich Residence — Budget Stay in Ladprao 71 with Pool and Free Parking
intro: If your brief is "stay in the Lat Phrao corridor, spend under ฿500 a night, and actually want a pool and free parking" — Fullrich Residence is one of the hardest combinations to match in this part of Bangkok. Tucked into Soi Nakniwat 21 off Ladprao 71, it sits around 1.5 km from MRT Yellow Line Chokchai 4 and offers 72 rooms, an outdoor pool, a children's pool, free on-site parking and free Wi-Fi. Rooms start from around ฿400/night — and the property carries a score of 7.1/10 from 825 reviews on Trip.com. That is an honest, mid-range number for a budget property, and we think it tells the story accurately.

body.html: What kind of place is this, and who is it for? Fullrich Residence makes no pretensions about being a boutique hotel or an Instagram backdrop. It is a functional, no-frills service residence that, according to the pattern of real guest reviews, draws three clear groups: workers temporarily stationed in the Lat Phrao corridor, budget travellers who arrive by car, and families or small groups who need a pool without paying mid-range prices. The building sits inside a quiet residential soi — the immediate neighbourhood is calm, removed from the noise of the main Lat Phrao road, which suits light sleepers well.

Location and getting around. The address is 9/122 Soi Nakniwat 21, Ladprao 71, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230. MRT Yellow Line Chokchai 4 station is around 1.5 km away — walkable in mild weather, but in Bangkok heat most guests take a motorbike taxi (around ฿10–15) or Grab. From Chokchai 4 you can ride the Yellow Line west to Central Plaza Ladprao and the Lat Phrao five-way intersection (with BTS and MRT interchange), or north toward Ramindra. Chokchai 4 street itself — one of Bangkok's most celebrated 24-hour street-food strips — is about 1 km away and makes a great dinner option. Heads-up from real reviewers: the soi is genuinely hard to find on your first visit. Save a Google Maps pin in advance and share it with your driver.
"The staff went out of their way to help — called taxis, ordered food for us, sorted everything. The pool is clean and quiet. For this price in Bangkok, it's a real find."

Rooms. There are 72 rooms across four categories. Cozy Studio (24 sq m, double bed) is the entry point for couples or solo travellers who want a proper room rather than a capsule. New Budget is the most affordable option, stripped to essentials. Deluxe 1-Bedroom (king bed) adds space and comfort for slightly more. Loft Suite (60 sq m, double bed plus two sofa beds) is the best pick for small groups or extended stays, and several reviewers specifically mentioned the balcony as a pleasant bonus. Every room comes with air conditioning, a fridge, a kettle, free Wi-Fi and a multi-channel TV. Critical note: there is no lift. Access to all upper floors is by stairs only. If you have heavy luggage, mobility concerns or a young child in a pushchair, request a ground- or first-floor room when booking and confirm again at check-in.

Facilities that stand out. The outdoor pool and children's pool are the main selling point at this price tier — reviewers consistently say the pool is clean and rarely crowded, which is refreshing for a budget property. Free parking is the second big draw: guests who drive up from the provinces for work or transit almost always highlight it. The property also has a fitness centre, a restaurant, laundry facilities, 24-hour front desk, bicycle rental and a small seminar room. Wi-Fi is free throughout the building, though a handful of reviews note that the signal weakens on upper floors — worth bearing in mind if you need a strong connection for remote work.
"Room isn't new but the sheets and towels were fresh. Pool was spotless. Parking was easy and free. At this price in Bangkok, I honestly expected less."

What real guests say — the full picture. Compiled from Trip.com (825 reviews, 7.1/10), TripAdvisor and HotelsCombined (aggregate 6.1/10, 738 reviews). On the positive side: friendly and proactive staff (repeatedly praised for calling taxis, ordering food and going beyond the basics), a clean and peaceful pool, spacious rooms particularly in the Loft Suite category, reliable free parking, and strong value relative to the price. On the critical side: the absence of a lift is the single most-mentioned practical issue, some rooms show their age with musty smells or mismatched photos online, a minority of reviews flag pest issues or maintenance delays, and staff English proficiency is limited — important for international guests who need detailed communication.

Pricing and value. New Budget and Cozy Studio rooms run approximately ฿380–500/night during regular periods, rising to ฿600–800 over public holidays, the New Year period and Songkran. Deluxe 1-Bedroom sits around ฿600–900 and the Loft Suite ฿900–1,200. For a property that includes an outdoor pool and free parking in the Lat Phrao area, the price-to-amenity ratio is genuinely competitive at the budget end. The honest caveat: if you need walkable BTS/MRT access, a lift or a freshly renovated room, the gap between expectation and reality may disappoint. But if your priority is a quiet base with a pool and free parking at a minimal cost, Fullrich delivers that reliably.

honestSummary: Fullrich Residence delivers an outdoor pool and free parking from around ฿400/night — a combination genuinely difficult to find in the Lat Phrao area. It suits car-travelling guests and multi-night stays best. The trade-offs are real: no lift, a soi location that takes effort to find, and rooms that show their age in places.

If you have heavy luggage or mobility limitations — there is no lift in the building. Request a ground- or first-floor room explicitly at the time of booking and confirm again at check-in.

If you expect rooms to match the promotional photos exactly — several reviewers found a gap between photos and reality, with some rooms appearing older or less maintained. Book a free-cancellation rate, inspect the room on arrival and ask to switch if needed.

faq.q: Where is Fullrich Residence in Bangkok, and how close is the MRT?
faq.a: Fullrich Residence is at 9/122 Soi Nakniwat 21, Ladprao 71, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230. MRT Yellow Line Chokchai 4 station is approximately 1.5 km away — a 5–7 minute motorbike taxi or a short Grab ride from the entrance of the soi.

faq.q: Does Fullrich Residence have a lift?
faq.a: No — there is no lift. All upper floors are accessed by stairs only. Guests with heavy luggage or mobility limitations should request a ground- or first-floor room when booking and confirm this preference at check-in.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Fullrich Residence Bangkok?
faq.a: New Budget and Cozy Studio rooms start from approximately ฿380–500/night in standard periods. Deluxe 1-Bedroom runs around ฿600–900 and the Loft Suite (60 sq m with balcony) around ฿900–1,200. Rates rise during public holidays, New Year and Songkran — book in advance to secure the best price.

faq.q: Does Fullrich Residence have a pool and free parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. The property has an outdoor swimming pool and a children's pool, which real guests consistently describe as clean and quiet. Free on-site parking is available for guests — inform the hotel at booking if you plan to arrive by car.

faq.q: Who is Fullrich Residence best for?
faq.a: It suits car-travelling guests, multi-night stays and budget travellers who want a pool without paying mid-range prices. It is less ideal for those relying solely on public transport, travelling with very heavy luggage, or expecting freshly renovated accommodation.
